briefing.headline: OpenAI Orion-2 and Anthropic Claude 4.5 push AGI benchmarks into new territory

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AGI race has intensified with multiple frontier labs releasing upgraded models this month. Compute constraints and safety concerns dominate strategic discussions among governments and corporations. Global AI investment remains at record levels despite regulatory headwinds.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed Orion-2 with multimodal reasoning gains while Anthropic released Claude 4.5. Google DeepMind and Meta continue scaling, with xAI and DeepSeek releasing competitive open-weight alternatives. Model capability gaps are narrowing rapidly across labs.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. Regulatory pressure is mounting on agentic deployments. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA Blackwell ramp and TSMC 2nm capacity allocations dominate chip news. Microsoft and Google announced new 100k GPU clusters in Europe and Asia. Energy and power grid constraints are emerging as primary bottlenecks.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will any single lab achieve AGI-level performance before 2028 or will the race remain multipolar?
